name: A Corner of Codimension Two Is Not Unique Through Seven Coordinates
statement: Let $X$ be ample on $q+2$ coordinates with $1\leq q\leq5$. If a corner has degree $q$, then it is not the unique corner of $X$.
proof: Translate a hypothetical unique corner to zero, use its $q$ incident directions as $F$, and call the other directions $u,v$. The four fibers are $Q_F,P,Q,C$. Isometry and uniqueness give $P\cup Q=Q_F\setminus\{0\}$ and exclude zero from $P,Q,C$. Relative peeling in at most five coordinates shows $P,Q\subseteq C$, hence $C=P\cup Q=Q_F\setminus\{0\}$ and both $P,Q$ are nonempty. Compare the $u=1$ face with the $u$-reduction. Their relative supports all contain $v$, so uniform inactive-coordinate removal reduces the interval to $Q\subseteq C$, which peels relatively. Lift this peeling to $X$, then peel the retained upper layer, the remaining $Q$-layer, and finally the root cube to zero. The first deletion supplies a corner distinct from the alleged unique corner.
